title: Compatible ordinary and derived presentations of the coefficient adjunction
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l and a scheme W on which l is invertible, with the project's independent universes and ordinary unbounded derived module categories. Use the fixed scalar-extension and coefficient-sequence functors. With OrdinaryModel and DerivedModel exactly as defined in [def-trf-completion-unit-models], there exist a coherent coefficient calculus S [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], its coherence witness, an OrdinaryModel M, and a DerivedModel for S and M. This is only the simultaneous construction and comparison-normalization assertion: it asserts no cone-augmentation formula, two-resolution unit formula or representative-independence theorem.

source.place: Tags 07A6, sites-cohomology.tex lemma-adjoint; 0D6E, sites-cohomology.tex lemma-derived-pushforward-composition; 0941, sites-cohomology.tex lemma-derived-limit-is-ok; 09T5, derived.tex lemma-derived-adjoint-functors; 03D7, sites-modules.tex lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules. The specified normalizations are the coefficient specialization in original completion-unit proof steps 1--4, not a verbatim assertion of these tags.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary simultaneous tensor system by the sequence projection theorem and strict-system/sequence-site equivalence. Its scalar-extension Hom bijections send b tensor x to b times the limit projection. Transport the right adjoint to the fixed coefficientSequenceRestriction followed by limit, using its sectionwise characterization. The unit is the family 1 tensor x; pure tensors determine the quotient transitions. Evaluation of the limit cone gives the termwise-limit comparison with the stated projections.

Choose S and its coherence from the coefficient-calculus existence theorem. Derive the ordinary adjunction on flat-term K-flat complexes and K-injectives. The normalized composition comparison identifies its right adjoint with the fixed coefficientSequenceLimit, without assuming restriction preserves K-injectives. Uniqueness of left adjoints compares its derived left adjoint with S.reduction, compatibly with the actual Hom equivalences. Transport the universal left-derived comparison and the resolving chain-map Hom equation along this isomorphism.

Check the finite evaluation comparison by taking the adjunction mates of the evaluated counits. S.counit_projection and the sequence pushforward/limit projected counit compute the same total-limit projection. The finite derived scalar-extension normalization on a flat-term K-flat representative therefore gives reduction_evaluation. This is equality of mates, not detection of arbitrary derived maps by their level components; S and its original coherence are retained.

The canonical unit of the right-derived constant-tower limit, transported through the degreewise limit comparison, gives limitUnit. Its K-injective normalization is the defining rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso equation. Exact countable pro-etale products give the strict Roos comparison; its unit normalization supplies roos_normalization. Derived composition gives systemUnit, its composition equation and invertibility on K-injectives. Assemble M and D. The same universal properties apply to zero inputs and unbounded complexes.
